questions.question: 20-year-old Renu is four times as old as her sister Kiran. After how many years will Renu become twice as old as Kiran?
questions.questionHtml: 20-year-old Renu is four times as old as her sister Kiran. After how many years will Renu become twice as old as Kiran?
questions.solution:
Given:

The age of Renu is = 20 years

Renu is four times as old as her sister Kiran:

(Kiran age) × 4 = Renu age

(Kiran age) × 4 = 20

Kiran's age = 5 years

Let after X years will Renu become twice as old as Kiran:

[(Renu's age + X) ÷ (Kiran's age + X)] = [(2) ÷ (1)]

[(20 + X) ÷ (5 + X)] = [(2) ÷ (1)]

(20 + X) = 2(5 + X)

(20 + X) = (10 + 2X)

X = 10 years

Here, after 10 years Renu will become twice as old as Kiran.

Hence, the correct answer is "10".

The correct answer is the value of money is rising.
Key Points
  • Inflation is the continuous rise in the price of a commodity. It reduces the purchasing power of the consumers and makes goods costlier.
  • Inflation helps to increase exports because goods become cheaper in the foreign market and reduces imports because goods become costlier in the domestic market.
  • Inflation increases the amount of money but reduces its value. It means that more amount of money has to be spent to get the same unit of quantity.

 Additional Information

  •  Types of inflation involve-
    • Demand-pull- When aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply in the economy. 
    • Cost-push- When price rises, due to a rise in any of the factors of production (land, labour, capital and entrepreneur).

Hence, the correct answer is that the value of money rising is not associated with inflation.

questions.question: The "Ministry of Jal Shakti" was formed by merging "Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation" along with?

The correct answer is Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.

Key Points

  • The Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed in May 2019 by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation and the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
  • This move aimed at integrating management of water resources and supply across India under a single umbrella ministry.
  • The Ministry of Jal Shakti focuses on issues related to water conservation, supply, management, and sanitation, including the implementation of flagship programs like the Jal Jeevan Mission.
  • The merger was part of the government’s efforts to streamline policies and strengthen the institutional framework for addressing water-related challenges in the country.
  • The Ministry also oversees the National Water Mission and other initiatives aimed at ensuring sustainable water use and equitable distribution.

Additional Information

  • Jal Jeevan Mission:
    • Launched in 2019, this mission aims to provide functional household tap connections (FHTC) to every rural household by 2024.
    • It emphasizes the importance of community participation in water resource management.
    • The program also focuses on water quality monitoring and capacity building at the village level.
  • National Water Mission:
    • This mission is part of India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).
    • Its objective is to conserve water, minimize waste, and ensure equitable distribution across regions.
    • The mission promotes the development of basin-level water resource management strategies.
  • Swachh Bharat Mission:
    • Previously implemented under the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation, now part of Jal Shakti Ministry.
    • It aims to eliminate open defecation and improve sanitation facilities across India.
    • The program has significantly contributed to improving hygiene and water-related health outcomes.
  • Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM):
    • This concept promotes coordinated development and management of water resources to maximize economic and social welfare.
    • The Ministry of Jal Shakti plays a key role in implementing IWRM strategies nationwide.

questions.question: The 'Arabian Sea Branch' and the 'Bay of Bengal Branch' are associated with which weather system in India?
questions.questionHtml: The 'Arabian Sea Branch' and the 'Bay of Bengal Branch' are associated with which weather system in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is South-West Monsoon.

Key Points

  • Arabian Sea Branch and Bay of Bengal Branch: These are the two distinct streams of the South-West Monsoon that originate and move across different regions of India.
  • The Arabian Sea Branch originates over the Arabian Sea and brings heavy rainfall to the western coast of India, including areas like Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, and Maharashtra. It is influenced by the Western Ghats, which enhance precipitation due to orographic lifting.
  • The Bay of Bengal Branch originates over the Bay of Bengal and moves towards the northeastern states like Assam, Meghalaya, and West Bengal. It also travels further north towards the Indo-Gangetic plains, bringing rainfall to regions like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab.
  • The South-West Monsoon is the primary monsoon system in India, responsible for approximately 75%-80% of the annual rainfall. It is critical for agriculture, water resources, and overall economic activities in the country. Hence, the correct answer is South-West Monsoon.

Additional Information

  • South-West Monsoon System:
    • It is characterized by the reversal of wind patterns due to the differential heating of land and water bodies. The monsoon winds blow from the south-west direction towards the Indian subcontinent.
    • The system is influenced by factors like the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), and the presence of high-pressure systems in the southern hemisphere.
  • Arabian Sea Branch:
    • This branch covers the western coast of India and brings heavy rainfall due to the Western Ghats. The orographic lifting of moist air causes intense precipitation in the region.
    • Examples of regions receiving rainfall from the Arabian Sea Branch include Kerala, Mumbai, and Mangalore.
  • Bay of Bengal Branch:
    • This branch moves towards the northeastern states and then spreads across the Indo-Gangetic plains. Rainfall is enhanced in regions with plains and foothills.
    • Example: States like Assam and Bihar receive rainfall due to this branch.
  • Agricultural Importance:
    • The South-West Monsoon is crucial for crops like rice, sugarcane, pulses, and cotton. Farmers depend heavily on monsoon rainfall for irrigation.
    • Regions like the Indo-Gangetic plains are highly dependent on monsoon rainfall for their agricultural economy.

Important Points

  • Other Weather Systems in India:
    • Pre-Monsoon: This period is characterized by localized thunderstorms, heat waves, and cyclonic activities, especially in April and May.
    • Tornadoes: Rare in India but can occur in regions like West Bengal and Odisha during extreme weather conditions.
    • North-East Monsoon: Occurs primarily in southern states like Tamil Nadu and brings rainfall during October to December.
  • Global Factors:
    • The El Niño and La Niña phenomena significantly influence monsoon behavior, leading to droughts or excessive rainfall.
    • The monsoon system is also affected by global warming and climate change, which can alter rainfall patterns.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Subhas Chandra Bose are correct? 1) He was elected President of the Indian National Congress at Tripuri session of 1938 A.D. 2) He escaped from home internment in January 1941 A.D. 3) On October 21 1943 A.D. he constituted the Provincial Government of India in Singapore.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements about Subhas Chandra Bose are correct?

1) He was elected President of the Indian National Congress at Tripuri session of 1938 A.D.

2) He escaped from home internment in January 1941 A.D.

3) On October 21 1943 A.D. he constituted the Provincial Government of India in Singapore.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Option 1. 

Key Points

  • Bose was elected Congress President at Haripura (1938), not Tripuri. The Tripuri session was in 1939 (where he was re-elected but soon resigned). Hence Statement 1 is Incorrect 
  • Bose made his “Great Escape” from house arrest in Calcutta in January 1941, traveling via Peshawar toward Germany. Hence Statement 2 is Correct. 
  • On 21 October 1943, Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) in Singapore. Hence the Statement 3 is Correct. 

Additional Information

  • Haripura 1938: Bose’s presidential address emphasized planning and industrialization; National Planning Committee idea gained momentum (Nehru later chaired).
  • Tripuri 1939: Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya; clash with the Gandhi-led group led to his resignation and formation of the Forward Bloc (1939).
  • Azad Hind Government (1943): Claimed authority over Andaman & Nicobar (renamed Shaheed and Swaraj); adopted the slogans “Jai Hind” and “Give me blood, I will give you freedom.”
  • INA (Azad Hind Fauj): Military wing revitalized under Bose; advanced to Imphal–Kohima front (1944) before retreat.

questions.question: Which of the following was/were the immediate reasons for the Royal Indian Navy mutiny in 1946? 1. Racial discrimination by British officers 2. Poor quality of food 3. Protest against the INA trial Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following was/were the immediate reasons for the Royal Indian Navy mutiny in 1946?

1. Racial discrimination by British officers

2. Poor quality of food

3. Protest against the INA trial

Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

Key Points

  • The Royal Indian Navy(RIN)revolt started on 18 February 1946 in Bombay.
  • The naval ratings on HMIS Talwar protested against the poor quality of food and racial discrimination by British officers. 
    • Hence statements 1 and 2 are correct.
  • The mutineers took out a procession in Bombay, holding aloft a portrait of Subhas Bose.
    • Their ships also raised the flags of the Congress, Muslim League, and Communist Party.
  • The demands advanced by the naval central strike committee combined service grievances with wider national concerns.
  • The latter included the release of INA (Indian National Army) personnel and other political prisoners; withdrawal of Indian troops from Indonesia; and the acceptance of Indian officers only as superiors.
    • ​Hence statement 3 is not correct.
  • The most significant feature of this short uprising was the massive outpouring of public support for the mutineers.
    • The city of Bombay, especially the labouring classes, went on strike on 22 February in solidarity.
      • The public transport network was brought to a halt, trains were burnt, roadblocks were erected and commercial establishments were shut down​

Additional Information

  • Naval Revolt of 1946
    • The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny started as a strike by ratings (a designation for a sailor subordinate to officers) demanding better food and accommodation.
    • The Indian sailors were treated badly by their British commanders and there were stark differences in the pay, living conditions, and basic amenities of Indians and British sailors in the navy.
    • The strike started in Bombay harbour where a contingent of ratings had arrived. The ratings of HMIS Talwar, a shore establishment also had seething discontent against their seniors for similar reasons.
    • On 19 February a Naval Central Strike committee was formed with Leading Signalman Lieutenant M.S. Khan and Petty Officer Telegraphist Madan Singh elected as president and vice-president respectively.
    • The strikers were inspired by the INA trials and the persona of Subhas Chandra Bose.
      • Soon, the strike evolved into open revolt with many cities joining the Bombay sailors.
      • Sailors from Karachi, Calcutta, Poona, Vizag, and Cochin joined involving 66 ships and shore establishments.
    • Ratings were not obeying their officers and they conducted demonstrations in the city of Bombay leaving their posts.
    • The city of Bombay particularly was tense.
      • Hundreds of protestors targeted the British residents and officers of the city.
      • They even took control of Butcher Island where the entire ammunition of the Bombay Presidency was stored.
    • The rebels also found support from the Royal Indian Air Force men from Bombay and from the Gurkhas in Karachi who, known for their loyalty, refused to fire at the strikers.
    • The open revolt struck at the heart of the British establishment who now realized that the armed forces, which was one of their key tools in maintaining their mastery over the subcontinent, could no longer be relied upon.
    • The sailors displayed a strong unity cutting across lines of religion and region despite the impending partition of the country on communal lines.
    • The revolt, however, failed to see support from the Indian leadership who perhaps saw a mutiny, so close to independence, as a danger.
      • Only the Communist Party of India and the INC’s Aruna Asaf Ali openly supported the sailors.
    • The mutiny came to an end with the intervention of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
      • The mutineers surrendered on 23 February 1946.
    • A total of 7 sailors and 1 officer were killed. 476 sailors were discharged as a result of the mutiny. They were not taken into the Indian or Pakistani navies after independence.
    • It is noteworthy to point out that there was massive public support for the mutineers. During the violence in Bombay that ensued because of the strike, over 200 civilians had died.​

questions.solution:
The correct answer is (A) is true but (R) is false.

Key Points

  • The word stupa means a mound.
  • While there are several kinds of stupas, round and tall, big and small, these have certain common features.
  • Generally, there is a small box placed at the centre or heart of the stupa.
  • This may contain bodily remains (such as teeth, bone or ashes) of the Buddha or his followers, or things they used, as well as precious stones, and coins.
  • This box, known as a relic casket, was covered with earth.
  • Later, a layer of mud brick or baked brick was added on top.
  • And then, the dome like structure was sometimes covered with carved stone slabs.
  • Often, a path, known as the pradakshina patha, was laid around the stupa. Hence, statement A is true.
  • This was surrounded with railings.
  • Entrance to the path was through gateways.
  • Devotees walked around the stupa, in a clockwise direction, as a mark of devotion. Thus, statement B is false.

  • Both railings and gateways were often decorated with sculpture.

Therefore, we can conclude that the correct answer is (A) is true but (R) is false.

    • It is introduced in Lok Sabha to draw the attention of the house to a definite matter of urgent public importance.
    • It involves a censure against the government.

  • No-Confidence motion 
    • Article 75 of the constitution says that the council of ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

Key Points

  • The tropical wet and dry climate is characterized by high temperatures throughout the year, typically above 18°C on average.
  • Rainfall is highly variable, with a distinct short wet season followed by a longer dry season.
  • This climate type is primarily found in regions located near the tropics, such as Sudan and Paraguay.
  • The tropical wet and dry climate is commonly associated with the savanna ecosystem, supporting grasslands interspersed with trees.
  • It is influenced by the movement of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), which brings seasonal shifts in rainfall.

Additional Information

  • Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):
    • ITCZ is a belt of low pressure that encircles the Earth near the equator.
    • It shifts north and south seasonally, influencing rainfall patterns in tropical regions.
  • Savanna Ecosystem:
    • Characterized by grasslands with scattered trees, it is common in tropical wet and dry climate regions.
    • Supports diverse flora and fauna, including herbivores like zebras and carnivores like lions.
  • Climate Classification:
    • As per the Köppen climate classification, tropical wet and dry climate is denoted as Aw.
    • It contrasts with tropical rainforest climates (Af) due to its distinct dry season.
  • Global Examples:
    • Besides Sudan and Paraguay, other regions with this climate include parts of Brazil, India, and northern Australia.
    • These areas often support agriculture and tourism based on their seasonal rainfall patterns.

questions.question: In the context of the Indian national movement, which of the following statements is correct regarding the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)? I. questions.questionHtml:
In the context of the Indian national movement, which of the following statements is correct regarding the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)?

I. It was founded in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla in Delhi.

Il. Subhas Chandra Bose and Bal Gangadhar Tilak were among the founder-members of the HSRA.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only I.

Key Points

  • The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi, as a revolutionary organization during the Indian independence movement.
  • HSRA was established by prominent freedom fighters such as Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Sukhdev Thapar, and others to promote socialist ideals and achieve independence through revolutionary activities.
  • The organization was formed after the Kakori Conspiracy Case of 1925, where some leaders of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) were arrested, and the remaining members reorganized it into the HSRA.
  • The goal of HSRA was to overthrow British colonial rule through armed struggle and establish a socialist state in India.
  • Subhas Chandra Bose and Bal Gangadhar Tilak were not associated with the founding of HSRA, as they were involved in other streams of the freedom movement.

Additional Information

  • Statement II:
    • Subhas Chandra Bose was primarily associated with the Indian National Congress and later founded the Forward Bloc. He was not involved with HSRA.
    • Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an early nationalist leader who played a key role in the extremist wing of the Congress. He passed away in 1920, much before the establishment of HSRA.
  • Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA):
    • The HSRA was a continuation of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), which was founded in 1924 by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, and others.
    • After the Kakori incident, Bhagat Singh and his comrades decided to add a socialist dimension to the group and renamed it HSRA.
    • The HSRA carried out several revolutionary acts, including the assassination of British police officer J.P. Saunders in 1928 as a retaliation for the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.
  • Socialist Ideals of HSRA:
    • The HSRA emphasized the need for socialism and economic equality to create a just society after independence.
    • It published a manifesto titled "Philosophy of the Bomb", explaining its revolutionary ideology and the justification for using violence as a means to achieve freedom.

    • Harishena: The court poet of Samudragupta composed the Prayaga Prashasti. Harishena not only served as a poet but also held an administrative position as a Mahadandanayaka (chief judicial and military officer).

    • Hence, statement 2 is correct.

questions.question: A sum lent at simple interest amounts to Rs.6,240.80 in one year and to Rs.7,563.20 in 4 years. The sum (in Rs.) and the rate of interest per annum, respectively, are:
questions.questionHtml: A sum lent at simple interest amounts to Rs.6,240.80 in one year and to Rs.7,563.20 in 4 years. The sum (in Rs.) and the rate of interest per annum, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since Simple Interest is constant every year, SI for 3 years = Amount4 − Amount1

⇒ 3 years SI = 7563.20 − 6240.80 = ₹1322.40

⇒ 1 year SI = 1322.40 ÷ 3 = ₹440.80

⇒ Principal = 6240.80 − 440.80 = ₹5800

⇒ Rate = (440.80 ÷ 5800) × 100 = 7.6%

∴ The correct answer is ₹5800, 7.6%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 1 year (A1) = ₹6240.80

Amount after 4 years (A4) = ₹7563.20

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

⇒ SI for 3 years = A4 − A1

⇒ SI for 3 years = 7563.20 − 6240.80 = 1322.40

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1322.40 ÷ 3 = 440.80

⇒ Principal (P) = A1 − SI for 1 year

⇒ P = 6240.80 − 440.80 = 5800

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (440.80 × 100) ÷ 5800

⇒ R = 44080 ÷ 5800 = 7.6%

∴ The correct answer is ₹5800, 7.6%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant every year, meaning the interest generated is the same annually. In Compound Interest, the accumulated interest of past periods is added to the principal to form the base for the next period.

Principal from Amounts Rule

If a principal becomes A1 in T1 years and A2 in T2 years under Simple Interest, the principal can be directly calculated as P = A1 − [ (A2 − A1) ÷ (T2 − T1) ] × T1.

Constant SI Property

Since Simple Interest does not compound, the interest accrued over any N-year period is always directly proportional to N, making it uniformly additive.

questions.question: In a business, the investment of Radhika is 37.5% more than that of Ridhima and the ratio of the investment of Ridhima and Ronita is 8 ∶ 7 and the ratio of the time period of the investments of Radhika, Ridhima and Ronita is 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 4 respectively. Find the ratio of profits received by Radhika, Ridhima and Ronita respectively.
questions.questionHtml: In a business, the investment of Radhika is 37.5% more than that of Ridhima and the ratio of the investment of Ridhima and Ronita is 8 ∶ 7 and the ratio of the time period of the investments of Radhika, Ridhima and Ronita is 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 4 respectively. Find the ratio of profits received by Radhika, Ridhima and Ronita respectively.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

37.5% = 3/8 ⇒ Investment of Radhika : Ridhima = 11 : 8.

Combined Investment (Radhika : Ridhima : Ronita) = 11 : 8 : 7.

Investment Time Ratio = 4 : 3 : 4.

Profit Ratio = (11 × 4) : (8 × 3) : (7 × 4) = 44 : 24 : 28.

Simplified Profit Ratio = 11 : 6 : 7.

∴ The correct option is D.

Alternate Method

Given:

Investment of Radhika = 137.5% of Ridhima investment.

Investment ratio Ridhima : Ronita = 8 : 7.

Time period ratio Radhika : Ridhima : Ronita = 4 : 3 : 4.

Formula Used:

Profit = Investment × Time Period

Calculations:

⇒ Let Ridhima investment = 8x.

⇒ Radhika investment = 8x + 37.5% of 8x = 8x + (3/8 × 8x) = 11x.

⇒ Ronita investment = 7x (since Ridhima : Ronita = 8 : 7).

⇒ Profit Ratio = (Radhika Inv × Time) : (Ridhima Inv × Time) : (Ronita Inv × Time).

⇒ Profit Ratio = (11x × 4) : (8x × 3) : (7x × 4).

⇒ Profit Ratio = 44 : 24 : 28.

⇒ Dividing each term by 4: 11 : 6 : 7.

∴ The correct option is D.

Additional Information

Partnership Ratio Rule

Profit of A : Profit of B = (CapitalA × TimeA) : (CapitalB × TimeB).

Calculation of Capital

If profit ratio and time ratio are given, Investment Ratio = (Profit ÷ Time)A : (Profit ÷ Time)B.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Standard values like 12.5% = 1/8, 25% = 1/4, and 37.5% = 3/8 help in fast ratio calculations.

questions.question: Akbar can complete a piece of work alone in 12 days, while Anthony can complete the same work alone in 20 days. If they work on alternate days with Anthony starting the work, then in how many days can they complete the whole work?
questions.questionHtml: Akbar can complete a piece of work alone in 12 days, while Anthony can complete the same work alone in 20 days. If they work on alternate days with Anthony starting the work, then in how many days can they complete the whole work?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work = LCM(12, 20) = 60 units.

Efficiency: Akbar = 5 units/day, Anthony = 3 units/day.

In a 2-day cycle (Anthony first, then Akbar), work done = 3 + 5 = 8 units.

In 7 cycles (14 days), work done = 7 × 8 = 56 units. Remaining work = 60 − 56 = 4 units.

Day 15: Anthony does 3 units. Remaining 1 unit is done by Akbar on Day 16 in 1/5 day.

∴ The correct answer is 15 1/5 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Akbar = 12 days

Time taken by Anthony = 20 days

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Akbar 12 60 60 ÷ 12 = 5
Anthony 20 60 ÷ 20 = 3

Calculations:

⇒ Total work is the LCM of 12 and 20 = 60 units.

⇒ Work done in the first 2 days = Anthony's efficiency + Akbar's efficiency = 3 + 5 = 8 units.

⇒ Number of complete 2-day cycles to reach near 60 = 60 ÷ 8 = 7 cycles (with 4 units remaining).

⇒ Time taken for 7 complete cycles = 7 × 2 = 14 days.

⇒ Work completed in 14 days = 7 × 8 = 56 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 56 = 4 units.

⇒ On the 15th day, it is Anthony's turn. He completes 3 units of work in 1 day.

⇒ Remaining work after 15th day = 4 − 3 = 1 unit.

⇒ On the 16th day, Akbar does the remaining 1 unit. Time taken by Akbar = 1 ÷ 5 = 1/5 day.

⇒ Total time taken = 14 + 1 + 1/5 = 15 1/5 days.

∴ The correct answer is 15 1/5 days.

Additional Information

Alternate Day Work

When workers work on alternate days, find the combined work done in one complete cycle (usually 2 days for two workers). Multiply the cycle to get as close to total work as possible without exceeding it, then calculate the remaining work day-by-day based on who started.

Pipes & Cisterns

Similar to time and work, but an outlet pipe performs negative work. Net work done in 1 hour = (1 ÷ Fill Time) − (1 ÷ Empty Time).

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person. If they work for the same number of days together, wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.question: A sum of ₹ 10,000 is lent partly at 12% and partly at 18% per annum simple interest. If the interest received after one year is ₹1530, then how much money was invested in rupees at 18% per annum?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of ₹ 10,000 is lent partly at 12% and partly at 18% per annum simple interest. If the interest received after one year is ₹1530, then how much money was invested in rupees at 18% per annum?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If the entire ₹10,000 was invested at 12%, the interest would be 12% of 10,000 = ₹1200.

Extra interest received = ₹1530 − ₹1200 = ₹330.

This extra interest is due to the additional 6% (18% − 12%) on the second part.

⇒ 6% of the amount invested at 18% = ₹330

⇒ Amount invested at 18% = (330 ÷ 6) × 100 = ₹5500

∴ The correct answer is ₹5500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Principal = ₹10,000

Total Simple Interest (SI) for 1 year = ₹1530

Formula Used:

Overall Rate of Interest = (SI × 100) ÷ (Principal × Time)

Calculation:

⇒ Overall Rate = (1530 × 100) ÷ (10000 × 1) = 15.3%

By applying the rule of Alligation:

⇒ Ratio of investments at 12% and 18% = (18 − 15.3) : (15.3 − 12)

⇒ Ratio = 2.7 : 3.3 = 27 : 33 = 9 : 11

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 9 + 11 = 20 parts

⇒ 20 parts = ₹10,000

⇒ 1 part = 10,000 ÷ 20 = ₹500

⇒ Amount invested at 18% (11 parts) = 11 × 500 = ₹5500

∴ The correct answer is ₹5500.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Formula

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of Interest, and T is Time period.

Rule of Alligation

When two ingredients of different prices or rates are mixed to produce a mixture, the ratio in which they are mixed is: (Cheaper Quantity) : (Dearer Quantity) = (Dearer Rate − Mean Rate) : (Mean Rate − Cheaper Rate).

Shift Method (Shortcut)

Assume the entire quantity is invested at the lower rate. The extra interest obtained is solely due to the percentage difference between the higher and lower rates on the second part. It saves time during competitive exams.

questions.question: The profit earned when an article is sold for Rs. 800 is 20 times the loss incurred when it is sold for Rs. 275. At what price should the article be sold if it is desired to make a profit of 25%.
questions.questionHtml: The profit earned when an article is sold for Rs. 800 is 20 times the loss incurred when it is sold for Rs. 275. At what price should the article be sold if it is desired to make a profit of 25%.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Profit to Loss = 20 : 1.

Total difference in SP = 800 − 275 = Rs. 525.

Value of 21 parts (Total Gap) = 525 ⇒ 1 part (Loss) = 525 ÷ 21 = Rs. 25.

Cost Price = Lower SP + Loss = 275 + 25 = Rs. 300.

New Selling Price for 25% profit = 300 × (125 ÷ 100) = Rs. 375.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 375.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price 1 (SP1) = Rs. 275 (sold at a loss)

Selling Price 2 (SP2) = Rs. 800 (sold at a profit)

Profit obtained = 20 × Loss incurred

Formula Used:

Loss = Cost Price (CP) − Selling Price

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price (CP)

Calculations:

⇒ Profit at SP2 = 20 × Loss at SP1

⇒ 800 − CP = 20 × (CP − 275)

⇒ 800 − CP = 20CP − 5500

⇒ 20CP + CP = 800 + 5500

⇒ 21CP = 6300

⇒ CP = 6300 ÷ 21 = Rs. 300

⇒ To make a 25% profit, the new selling price must be 125% of the Cost Price.

⇒ New Selling Price = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ New Selling Price = 300 × (125 ÷ 100)

⇒ New Selling Price = 300 × 1.25 = Rs. 375

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 375.

Additional Information

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. The fundamental formula is: Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is calculated as: a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight, the actual Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.

questions.question: If x is subtracted from each of 52, 47, 20 and 19, the number so obtained in this order are in proportion. What is the mean proportional between (x + 13) and (x - 8)?
questions.questionHtml: If x is subtracted from each of 52, 47, 20 and 19, the number so obtained in this order are in proportion. What is the mean proportional between (x + 13) and (x - 8)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For numbers a, b, c, d to be in proportion when x is subtracted: x = (ad − bc) ÷ ((a + d) − (b + c))

Here, a = 52, b = 47, c = 20, d = 19

x = (52 × 19 − 47 × 20) ÷ ((52 + 19) − (47 + 20)) = (988 − 940) ÷ (71 − 67) = 48 ÷ 4 = 12

Mean proportional between (x + 13) and (x − 8) = √((12 + 13) × (12 − 8)) = √(25 × 4) = √100 = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numbers: 52, 47, 20, 19

When x is subtracted from each, they become proportional.

Formula Used:

If a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then a ÷ b = c ÷ d.

Mean proportional between two numbers p and q = √(p × q)

Calculations:

⇒ (52 − x) : (47 − x) :: (20 − x) : (19 − x)

⇒ (52 − x) ÷ (47 − x) = (20 − x) ÷ (19 − x)

⇒ (52 − x)(19 − x) = (20 − x)(47 − x)

⇒ 988 − 52x − 19x + x2 = 940 − 20x − 47x + x2

⇒ 988 − 71x = 940 − 67x

⇒ 71x − 67x = 988 − 940

⇒ 4x = 48

⇒ x = 12

Now, finding the given terms to calculate the mean proportional:

⇒ First term = (x + 13) = 12 + 13 = 25

⇒ Second term = (x − 8) = 12 − 8 = 4

⇒ Mean proportional = √(25 × 4) = √100 = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b). It represents the value x such that a : x :: x : b.

Third Proportional

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then c is the third proportional to a and b. Formula: c = b2 ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional is x such that a : b :: c : x. Formula: x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a ÷ b = c ÷ d, then applying Componendo and Dividendo gives (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d). This rule is widely used to simplify complex ratios.

questions.questionHtml: The difference between the interest payable on a sum invested for three years at 20% compound interest per annum compounded annually and 20% simple interest per annum for the same period is ₹448. What is the value of the sum invested?

questions.question: The cost of painting 4 walls and ceiling is Rs. 12750. If the length of the room is 5 m more than the breadth of the room and the height of the room is 3 m, the price of the painting is Rs. 25 per m 2 , then find the length of the room.
questions.questionHtml: The cost of painting 4 walls and ceiling is Rs. 12750. If the length of the room is 5 m more than the breadth of the room and the height of the room is 3 m, the price of the painting is Rs. 25 per m<sup>2</sup>, then find the length of the room.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total area to be painted = Total Cost ÷ Rate = 12750 ÷ 25 = 510 m2.

Area of 4 walls + ceiling = 2h(l + b) + lb = 510.

Given h = 3 m and l = b + 5.

Using Option 2: If length (l) = 20 m, then breadth (b) = 15 m.

Painted Area = 2 × 3 × (20 + 15) + (20 × 15) = 210 + 300 = 510 m2 (Matches the given area).

∴ The correct answer is 20 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of painting = Rs. 12750

Rate of painting = Rs. 25 per m2

Height of the room (h) = 3 m

Let the breadth of the room be b meters.

Length of the room (l) = (b + 5) meters

Formula Used:

Area of 4 walls and ceiling = 2h(l + b) + lb

Calculations:

⇒ Total Painted Area = Total Cost ÷ Rate

⇒ Area = 12750 ÷ 25 = 510 m2

⇒ 2 × 3 × (b + 5 + b) + (b + 5) × b = 510

⇒ 6 × (2b + 5) + b2 + 5b = 510

⇒ 12b + 30 + b2 + 5b = 510

⇒ b2 + 17b + 30 − 510 = 0

⇒ b2 + 17b − 480 = 0

⇒ b2 + 32b − 15b − 480 = 0

⇒ b(b + 32) − 15(b + 32) = 0

⇒ (b − 15)(b + 32) = 0

⇒ b = 15 or b = −32

Since the breadth cannot be negative, we have b = 15 m.

⇒ Length of the room (l) = b + 5 = 15 + 5 = 20 m

∴ The correct answer is 20 m.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area includes all 6 faces and is calculated as 2(lb + bh + hl).

Lateral Surface Area of Cuboid

The area of only the 4 walls (excluding ceiling and floor) is given by 2h(l + b).

Volume of a Cuboid

The internal space enclosed by a cuboid is calculated using the formula Volume = l × b × h.

Length of Diagonal

The longest dimension within a cuboidal room is its main diagonal, given by √(l2 + b2 + h2).

questions.question: A shopkeeper announced a festival discount of 30% for all the items in his shop. Vijay bought a mobile phone. He got a discount of Rs. 960. What was the list price of the mobile phone ?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper announced a festival discount of 30% for all the items in his shop. Vijay bought a mobile phone. He got a discount of Rs. 960. What was the list price of the mobile phone ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By equating the given discount percentage directly to the discount value:

⇒ 30% → Rs. 960

⇒ 1% → Rs. 960 ÷ 30 = Rs. 32

⇒ 100% (List Price) → Rs. 32 × 100 = Rs. 3200

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3200.

Alternate Method

Given:

Festival Discount = 30%

Discount Amount = Rs. 960

Formula Used:

Discount = (Discount Percentage ÷ 100) × List Price

Calculations:

⇒ Let the List Price of the mobile phone be x.

⇒ 30% of x = 960

⇒ (30 ÷ 100) × x = 960

⇒ x = (960 × 100) ÷ 30

⇒ x = 32 × 100

⇒ x = 3200

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3200.

Additional Information

Marked Price (List Price)

It is the original price printed on an article or item tag. Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price.

Selling Price Formula

Selling Price = Marked Price × ((100 − Discount %) ÷ 100).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d1% and d2% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: (d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2) ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: Let ‘m' and 'n' be two positive integers such that m + n + mn = 118, then the value of 'm + n' is -
questions.questionHtml: Let ‘m' and 'n' be two positive integers such that m + n + mn = 118, then the value of 'm + n' is -
questions.solution:
Adding 1 on both sides,

⇒ m + n + mn + 1 = 118 + 1

→ m + mn + n + 1 = 119 → m (1 + n) + 1(1 + n) = 17 * 7

→ (m + 1) (1 + n) = 17 * 7 → m + 1 = 17

→ m = 17 - 1 = 16

⇒ 1 + n = 7

→ n = 7 - 1 = 6

⇒ m + n = 16 + 6

→ m + n = 22

questions.question: If \(\sqrt{14.44}\) + \(\sqrt{(9 + x^2)}\) = 8.8, then find the value of x.
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sqrt{14.44}\) + \(\sqrt{(9 + x^2)}\) = 8.8, then find the value of x.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since 382 = 1444, √14.44 = 3.8.

3.8 + √(9 + x2) = 8.8

√(9 + x2) = 8.8 − 3.8 = 5

Squaring: 9 + x2 = 25 ⇒ x2 = 16

x = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method

Given: √14.44 + √(9 + x2) = 8.8

Formula used: √a = b ⇒ a = b2

Calculation:

⇒ √(1444/100) + √(9 + x2) = 8.8

⇒ 3.8 + √(9 + x2) = 8.8

⇒ √(9 + x2) = 8.8 − 3.8

⇒ √(9 + x2) = 5

⇒ 9 + x2 = 52

⇒ 9 + x2 = 25

⇒ x2 = 25 − 9 = 16

⇒ x = √16

⇒ x = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information

Square Root of Decimals

For a decimal number, the square root contains half the number of decimal places of the original number (e.g., √0.01 = 0.1).

Pythagorean Triplets

The equation 32 + x2 = 52 represents a standard (3, 4, 5) right-angled triangle triplet where x = 4.

Perfect Squares

Knowing squares up to 40 helps in speed calculation. For instance, 382 = 1444 and 392 = 1521.

questions.question: If x/y = 4/7 and 5x + 4y = 15, then find the value of x.
questions.questionHtml: If x/y = 4/7 and 5x + 4y = 15, then find the value of x.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given the ratio x : y = 4 : 7, assume x = 4k and y = 7k.

Substitute these values into the second equation: 5(4k) + 4(7k) = 15

⇒ 20k + 28k = 15

⇒ 48k = 15 ⇒ k = 15/48 = 5/16

Now find x: x = 4 × (5/16) = 5/4 = 1.25

∴ The correct answer is 1.25.

Alternate Method

Given:

x/y = 4/7

5x + 4y = 15

Calculations:

⇒ From the ratio x/y = 4/7, let x = 4k and y = 7k.

⇒ Substitute the values of x and y in the linear equation:

⇒ 5(4k) + 4(7k) = 15

⇒ 20k + 28k = 15

⇒ 48k = 15

⇒ k = 15 ÷ 48

⇒ k = 5/16

⇒ Substitute the value of k back to find x:

⇒ x = 4k = 4 × (5/16)

⇒ x = 5/4

⇒ x = 1.25

∴ The correct answer is 1.25.

Additional Information

Ratio & Proportion Rule

If two quantities are in the ratio a:b, they can be represented as ax and bx where x is a common constant multiplier. This allows reducing two variables into a single variable.

Substitution Method

In solving linear equations, isolating one variable in terms of the other and substituting it into the second equation easily determines the unknown single variable.

questions.question: Find the value of (cot \(\frac{α}{2}\) tanα - 1) (2 - tanα.sin2α) =?
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of (cot\(\frac{α}{2}\) tanα - 1) (2 - tanα.sin2α) =?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put α = 60°.

First bracket: cot(60°/2) × tan60° − 1 = cot30° × tan60° − 1 = √3 × √3 − 1 = 2.

Second bracket: 2 − tan60° × sin120° = 2 − √3 × (√3/2) = 2 − 3/2 = 1/2.

Result = 2 × 1/2 = 1.

Checking options for α = 60°, only Option 3 yields 2cos60° = 2 × 1/2 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 2cosα.

Alternate Method

Given:

(cot(α/2) tanα − 1) (2 − tanα sin2α)

Calculations:

Simplify the first bracket:

⇒ cot(α/2) = cos(α/2) / sin(α/2)

⇒ tanα = sinα / cosα = [2sin(α/2) cos(α/2)] / cosα

⇒ cot(α/2) tanα = [cos(α/2) / sin(α/2)] × [2sin(α/2) cos(α/2) / cosα]

⇒ cot(α/2) tanα = 2cos2(α/2) / cosα

⇒ Using half-angle formula, 2cos2(α/2) = 1 + cosα

⇒ First bracket = (1 + cosα) / cosα − 1 = (1 / cosα) + 1 − 1 = 1 / cosα

Simplify the second bracket:

⇒ 2 − tanα sin2α

⇒ 2 − (sinα / cosα) × (2sinα cosα)

⇒ 2 − 2sin2α

⇒ 2(1 − sin2α) = 2cos2α

Multiply both simplified parts:

⇒ Result = (1 / cosα) × 2cos2α

⇒ Result = 2cosα

∴ The correct answer is 2cosα.

Additional Information

Double Angle Formulas

sin2α = 2sinα cosα | cos2α = cos2α − sin2α = 2cos2α − 1 = 1 − 2sin2α

Half Angle Formulas

1 − cosα = 2sin2(α/2) | 1 + cosα = 2cos2(α/2)

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin2α + cos2α = 1 | sec2α − tan2α = 1

questions.question: Find the sum of all two digit numbers that give a remainder 3 when they are divided by 8.
questions.questionHtml: Find the sum of all two digit numbers that give a remainder 3 when they are divided by 8.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The smallest 2-digit number leaving a remainder 3 when divided by 8 is 11, and the largest is 99.

These numbers form an Arithmetic Progression (AP) with a common difference of 8.

Total number of terms (n) = [(99 − 11) ÷ 8] + 1 = 12

Sum = (n ÷ 2) × (First term + Last term)

Sum = (12 ÷ 2) × (11 + 99) = 6 × 110 = 660

∴ The correct answer is 660.

Alternate Method

Given:

The numbers are two-digit numbers that leave a remainder 3 when divided by 8.

Formula Used:

Sum of an AP = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l)

Where a = first term, l = last term, and n = number of terms.

Calculations:

⇒ General form of the given numbers = 8k + 3

⇒ For two-digit numbers, the range is: 10 ≤ 8k + 3 ≤ 99

⇒ Subtracting 3 from all sides: 7 ≤ 8k ≤ 96

⇒ Dividing by 8: 0.875 ≤ k ≤ 12

⇒ The possible integer values for k are 1, 2, 3, ..., 12

⇒ First term (a) at k = 1 is 8 × 1 + 3 = 11

⇒ Last term (l) at k = 12 is 8 × 12 + 3 = 99

⇒ Total number of terms (n) = 12

⇒ Sum of these terms = (12 ÷ 2) × (11 + 99)

⇒ Sum = 6 × 110 = 660

∴ The correct answer is 660.

Additional Information

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence of numbers in which the difference of any two successive members is a constant. The general term is given by Tn = a + (n − 1)d.

Sum of an AP

The sum of the first n terms can be calculated using Sn = (n ÷ 2) × [2a + (n − 1)d] or Sn = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l) when the first and last terms are known.

Number of Terms in an AP

If the first term a, the last term l, and the common difference d are known, the number of terms is n = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1.

questions.question: The ratio of the expenditure of A, B, C are 207 : 195 : 217 respectively and their savings are 10%, 25% and 30% of their income. If the sum of their income is Rs. 4,000, Find the difference between the income of A and C.
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the expenditure of A, B, C are 207 : 195 : 217 respectively and their savings are 10%, 25% and 30% of their income. If the sum of their income is Rs. 4,000, Find the difference between the income of A and C.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Income ratio = Expenditure Ratio ÷ Expenditure %

Income ratio = (207 ÷ 90) : (195 ÷ 75) : (217 ÷ 70) = 2.3 : 2.6 : 3.1 = 23 : 26 : 31

Total Income = 23 + 26 + 31 = 80 units

∴ 80 units = 4000 ⇒ 1 unit = 50

Difference between A and C = (31 − 23) units = 8 × 50 = 400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expenditure ratio of A : B : C = 207 : 195 : 217

Savings % of A = 10%, B = 25%, C = 30%

Sum of their incomes = Rs. 4000

Formula Used:

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Expenditure % = 100% − Savings %

Calculations:

⇒ Expenditure % of A = 100% − 10% = 90%

⇒ Expenditure % of B = 100% − 25% = 75%

⇒ Expenditure % of C = 100% − 30% = 70%

⇒ Let the incomes of A, B and C be IA, IB, and IC.

⇒ 90% of IA : 75% of IB : 70% of IC = 207 : 195 : 217

⇒ IA = (207 × 100) ÷ 90 = 230

⇒ IB = (195 × 100) ÷ 75 = 260

⇒ IC = (217 × 100) ÷ 70 = 310

⇒ Ratio of Incomes = 230 : 260 : 310 = 23 : 26 : 31

⇒ Total Income units = 23 + 26 + 31 = 80 units

⇒ 80 units = Rs. 4000 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 50

⇒ Difference between income of C and A = (31 − 23) units = 8 units

⇒ Required difference = 8 × 50 = Rs. 400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400.

Additional Information

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The foundational relationship governing an individual's personal finance is: Income = Expenditure + Savings. If savings are given as a percentage of total income, the expenditure percentage is directly found by subtracting the savings percentage from 100%.

Ratio Comparison Trick

When the ratios of expenditures and their respective percentages are known, the underlying base values (incomes) can be efficiently found by simply dividing each ratio value by its corresponding percentage value. Ratio of bases = Ratio1 ÷ P1 : Ratio2 ÷ P2.

Compound Ratio Distribution

When partitioning a total quantity according to a combined ratio, the value of 1 fundamental unit equals the total given quantity divided by the aggregate sum of all parts in the ratio. Target portion = Specific Ratio Unit × Value of 1 Unit.

questions.question: The average weight of some students in the class is 38 kg, when 4 new students are added, the average weight becomes 39.5 kg and the weight of those 4 students becomes 46, 52, 36 and 42 kg. Find the total number of students in the class including 4 new students.
questions.questionHtml: The average weight of some students in the class is 38 kg, when 4 new students are added, the average weight becomes 39.5 kg and the weight of those 4 students becomes 46, 52, 36 and 42 kg. Find the total number of students in the class including 4 new students.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average weight of the 4 new students = (46 + 52 + 36 + 42) ÷ 4 = 176 ÷ 4 = 44 kg.

Deviation of the new students' average from the original average = 44 − 38 = +6 kg per student.

Total extra weight added by the 4 new students = 4 × 6 = 24 kg.

This 24 kg extra weight raises the overall average of the entire class by 1.5 kg (from 38 to 39.5).

Total number of students = Total Extra Weight ÷ Increase in Average = 24 ÷ 1.5 = 16.

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial average weight of the class = 38 kg

Weights of the 4 new students = 46 kg, 52 kg, 36 kg, and 42 kg

New average weight of the class = 39.5 kg

Formula Used:

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial number of students in the class be n.

⇒ Total initial weight of students = 38 × n = 38n kg

⇒ Total weight of the 4 new students = 46 + 52 + 36 + 42 = 176 kg

⇒ New total weight of all students = (38n + 176) kg

⇒ Total number of students now = n + 4

⇒ New average = (38n + 176) ÷ (n + 4)

⇒ 39.5 = (38n + 176) ÷ (n + 4)

⇒ 39.5 × (n + 4) = 38n + 176

⇒ 39.5n + 158 = 38n + 176

⇒ 39.5n − 38n = 176 − 158

⇒ 1.5n = 18

⇒ n = 18 ÷ 1.5

⇒ n = 12

⇒ Total number of students including the 4 new ones = n + 4 = 12 + 4 = 16

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Additional Information

Averages

The average (or arithmetic mean) of a given data set is calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Combined Average

When two groups with counts n1 and n2 and individual averages A1 and A2 are combined, their overall average is obtained using: Combined Average = (n1 × A1 + n2 × A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Net Deviation Method

A powerful shortcut for calculating changes in averages. The change in the average is strictly equal to the net extra (or deficit) value added, divided entirely across the total number of participants: Increase in Average = Net Deviation ÷ Total Count.

questions.question: The ages of Ram and Mohan are in the ratio of 5 : 7 and the difference between them is 12 years. The ages (in years) of Ram and Mohan are respectively:
questions.questionHtml: The ages of Ram and Mohan are in the ratio of 5 : 7 and the difference between them is 12 years. The ages (in years) of Ram and Mohan are respectively:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in ratio parts = 7 − 5 = 2 parts.

2 parts → 12 years.

1 part → 6 years.

Ram's age = 5 parts = 5 × 6 = 30 years.

Mohan's age = 7 parts = 7 × 6 = 42 years.

∴ The correct answer is 30, 42 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of the ages of Ram and Mohan = 5 : 7

Difference between their ages = 12 years

Calculation:

⇒ Let the present ages of Ram and Mohan be 5x and 7x respectively.

⇒ According to the given condition, the difference in their ages is 12 years.

⇒ 7x − 5x = 12

⇒ 2x = 12

⇒ x = 12 ÷ 2 = 6

⇒ Present age of Ram = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30 years

⇒ Present age of Mohan = 7x = 7 × 6 = 42 years

∴ The correct answer is 30, 42 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The age difference between any two individuals always remains constant regardless of the number of years passed (past or future).

Ratio & Proportion Principle

If two quantities are in the ratio a : b, their exact values can be expressed as ax and bx, where x represents a common multiplier.

Sum & Difference Shortcut

When the ratio of two numbers is a : b, the absolute value of 1 ratio part = Difference ÷ (a − b) or Sum ÷ (a + b).

questions.question: A right circular cone of height 15 cm and base radius 15 cm is carved out of a wooden sphere of radius 15 cm . Volume of the remaining wood (in %) is:
questions.questionHtml: A right circular cone of height 15 cm and base radius 15 cm is carved out of a wooden sphere of radius 15 cm. Volume of the remaining wood (in %) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the cone's radius and height are equal to the sphere's radius (R = r = h = 15 cm):

Volume of Cone = (1/3) × π × R3

Volume of Sphere = (4/3) × π × R3

Percentage of volume removed = [(1/3) ÷ (4/3)] × 100 = 25%

Remaining volume = 100% − 25% = 75%

∴ The correct answer is 75%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the sphere (R) = 15 cm

Radius of the cone (r) = 15 cm

Height of the cone (h) = 15 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of a Sphere = (4/3) × πR3

Volume of a Cone = (1/3) × πr2h

⇒ Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × π × (15)3

⇒ Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × π × 3375 = 4500π cm3

⇒ Volume of the carved out cone = (1/3) × π × (15)2 × 15

⇒ Volume of the carved out cone = (1/3) × π × 3375 = 1125π cm3

⇒ Volume of the remaining wood = 4500π − 1125π = 3375π cm3

⇒ Percentage of remaining wood = (Remaining Volume ÷ Total Volume) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (3375π ÷ 4500π) × 100

⇒ Percentage = 0.75 × 100 = 75%

∴ The correct answer is 75%.

Additional Information

Volume of a Sphere

The formula for the volume of a sphere is V = (4/3)πr3, and its total surface area is 4πr2.

Volume of a Cone

The formula for the volume of a right circular cone is V = (1/3)πr2h, and its curved surface area is πrl, where l = √(r2 + h2).

Percentage Remaining

When a part of a solid is removed, the remaining percentage is calculated as: [(Total Volume − Removed Volume) ÷ Total Volume] × 100.

questions.question: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Shami is (best) than Chahal.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.

Shami is (best) than Chahal.
questions.solution:
The most suitable adjective is better.

Key Points

  • The three words—good, better, and best—are examples of the three forms of an adjective or adverb: positive, comparative, and superlative.
  • The positive form of an adjective or adverb is the basic form listed in a dictionary.
  • The comparative form is used when there is a comparison between two or more things. It is succeeded by the preposition 'than'.
  • The superlative form is used for the highest kind, quality, or order; surpassing all else or others; supreme; extreme. It is preceded by the article 'the'.
  • Example:
    • She is a good Cricketer.
    • Rohit is a better human being than his brother.
    • He is the best singer in our class.
  • Since the comparative term (than) has been used after the underlined part, the adjective 'better' will be used in the underlined part.
     

Correct Sentence: Shami is better than Chahal.

Additional Information

  • Whenever we see the structure like 'as....as' and 'so....as', we will use a positive degree of adjective/adverb.
  • For example:
    • The thief ran as faster as he could.
    • The thief ran as fast as he could.

Key PointsWe need to make some changes in order to convert the direct sentence into indirect form if the second part of the sentence i.e. reported speech is in question form.
  • Convert 'said to' into 'asked' 
  • Remove inverted comma and question mark. 
  • In the sentence, change the subject of the second part (reported speech) on the basis of the subject & object of the first part(reporting speech).
  • In the sentence, change the tense of the second part on the basis of the tense that is used in the first part.
When we consider the above-written changes and try to change the given sentence into indirect form, the sentence would be:
'The owner of the house asked the tenant when he would pay the rent for that month.' 
Hence, the correct answer is Option 3.

  • Superlative adjectives: Superlative adjectives describe one person or thing as having more of a quality than all other people or things in a group.

    • Example: I think that’s the biggest apple I’ve ever seen!

questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In this section, each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and the sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1 :  The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) was established in 1975.

S6 : These predictions have an effect on the Indian economy that belies any belief that the economy of our country is not solely dependent on agriculture and the rains that feed it.

P : The Meteorological Department is perhaps also burdened with the most critical form of soothsaying i.e., forecasting the monsoon.

Q : The Crop Yield Formation Unit of the department has developed statistical models using correlation and regression techniques.

R : The IMD issued the first operational long range forecast of seasonal south-west monsoon rainfall in India in 1986.

S : It is the natural meteorological service and the principal agency in all matters related to meteorology.

The correct sequence should be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'SRQP.'

Key Points

  • While arranging the parts of the passage given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them, so let’s find out.  
    • The first statement in the sequence should be the one that best connects with S1.
    • It should be a continuation or extension of S1.
    • S follows S1 because it is adding information about the natural meteorological service, explained in S1.
    • R follows S because it is adding more information to S.
    • P is directly connected to S6 as P is talking about forecasting the monsoon.
  • Therefore, the sequence is 'S1SRQPS6.'
  • ​​The correct sequence:
    ​

S1 :  The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) was established in 1975.

S : It is the natural meteorological service and the principal agency in all matters related to meteorology.

R : The IMD issued the first operational long range forecast of seasonal south-west monsoon rainfall in India in 1986.

Q : The Crop Yield Formation Unit of the department has developed statistical models using correlation and regression techniques.

P : The Meteorological Department is perhaps also burdened with the most critical form of soothsaying i.e., forecasting the monsoon.

S6 : These predictions have an effect on the Indian economy that belies any belief that the economy of our country is not solely dependent on agriculture and the rains that feed it.

Additional Information   
 
  
 
 
 

  • Steps for solving Para Jumbles:
    • Clues include pronouns, like he, she, it, this, that, these, those; adverbs like formally, really; article a, an and the; definers like actually, finally, another; connectors like but, yet, both, also and neither nor, or, however, nevertheless.
    • Now, with the help of clues, try to find out qualifier and qualified sentences, so that we can make pairs of qualified and qualifier sentences to eliminate the wrong choices given in the question.
    • After making pairs, start eliminating the wrong choices or options given in the question.
    • In case there is more than one choice, try to follow the sequence of sentences according to the occurrence of the events.

Hinglish   

  • विकल्पों में दिए गए गद्यांश के भागों को व्यवस्थित करते समय, हमें उनके बीच कुछ व्याकरणिक या प्रासंगिक संबंध खोजने होंगे, तो आइए जानें।
  • अनुक्रम में पहला कथन वह होना चाहिए जो S1 के साथ सर्वोत्तम रूप से जुड़ता हो।
  • यह S1 की निरंतरता या विस्तार होना चाहिए।
  • S, S1 का अनुसरण करता है क्योंकि यह natural meteorological service के बारे में जानकारी जोड़ रहा है, जिसे S1 में समझाया गया है।

  • To convert to active voice: The subject performing the action is implied (e.g., “you” or “anyone”), and the sentence is restructured to directly state the action.
  • The correct active voice sentence is: "Submit the completed application form at the registration counter before the final deadline."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "Submit the completed application form at the registration counter before the final deadline."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "You should submit the completed application form at the registration counter before the final deadline." – Adds “should,” which is not implied in the original sentence.
  • Option 3: "You must submit the completed application form at the registration counter before the final deadline." – Adds “must,” which changes the tone of the instruction.
  • Option 4: "You will submit the completed application form at the registration counter before the final deadline." – Incorrect tense; “will” is not implied in the original sentence.

questions.question: This question consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Rearrange the sentences and choose the correct option. S1: For a long time, I could not decide whether I should speak to her or not. S6: At last I moved my lips and told her that her father had passed away. P: She was anxious to know about her father. Q: I knew she would start weeping. R: She looked towards me with anxious eyes. S: I could not tell her that her father had died before the doctor arrived.
questions.questionHtml:
This question consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Rearrange the sentences and choose the correct option.

S1: For a long time, I could not decide whether I should speak to her or not.
S6: At last I moved my lips and told her that her father had passed away.
P: She was anxious to know about her father.
Q: I knew she would start weeping.
R: She looked towards me with anxious eyes.
S: I could not tell her that her father had died before the doctor arrived.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'SQRP.'  Key Points 

  • By reading the above-given options we can understand that the author wants to tell something to a girl.
  • Part S will come first, as it shows why the author was not able to speak to her.
  • Q will come next, as it shows the possible outcome of the author's action.
  • P will follow R, as it shows why she was looking anxiously at the author.
  • Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

The correct sequence is:
S1: For a long time, I could not decide whether I should speak to her or not.
S: I could not tell her that her father had died before the doctor arrived.
Q: I knew she would start weeping.
R: She looked towards me with anxious eyes.
​P: She was anxious to know about her father.
S6: At last I moved my lips and told her that her father had passed away.Important Points   

  • Here are some tips to solve the para jumbles:
    • You need to understand the idea behind the paragraph. If you can understand the idea/theme of the paragraph it is easy to put the sentences in order then.
    • You should look out for the starting or the concluding sentences in the question. Sometimes they are clearly visible and can help you immensely in identifying the correct sequence.
    • You need to know the relationships between different sentences to put them in the right sequence. 
    • You should first fix the relationships of sentences, put them in order and then check the options.
    • Transition words and contrasting words also help in finding clean relationships between sentences of the sentence rearrangement.
    • Do not over depend on options, they only confuse you if you keep looking at them, use them as facilitators only, especially to fix your first sentence.
    • The whole paragraph should have a coherent idea and flow when arranged in the correct order.

  • There are some verbs that take fixed prepositions with them.

Additional Information

  • A gerund is a verb that’s acting as a noun. By that, we mean that the verb—the word that describes the action that’s happening, like “biking,” “thinking,” “running,” or “speaking”—becomes a thing, a concept that can now be the sentence’s subject, direct object, indirect object, or the object of a preposition. 
  • It doesn’t stop being a verb, but the role it plays in a sentence shifts from describing the action to being a focal point. 
  • Here are two examples of sentences that contain gerunds:
    • As a food blogger, eating is an involved production for Shoshanna. 
    • Fazal turned off his phone and shut the door so he could focus on studying.

6. Nostalgia took me to the depths of past
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
Key Points
  • The paragraph begins by introducing the concept of time, highlighting its power and fleeting nature.
  • Sentence R is the first sentence as it directly follows the idea of time being powerful and fleeting:
    • "It flees with the blink of an eye."

  • The correct sequence is RQPS.
